latest_release.name: h5i v0.5.6
latest_release.body:
## Install

One binary. `h5i` unifies web development, formal verification
with Lean 4, and red-teaming around a composable Rust framework.

**Linux / macOS:**
```bash
curl -L https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/releases/download/v0.5.6/h5i-v0.5.6-<TARGET>.tar.gz | tar -xz
sudo mv h5i /usr/local/bin/
```

**Windows:** download the `.zip`, extract `h5i.exe`, and add it to your `PATH`.

### The browser

```bash
h5i browser open https://example.com
h5i browser snapshot
h5i browser requests     # what it asked for, and what was refused
h5i browser audit        # the whole session, afterwards
```

A session is Chromium, driven through
[agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser)
(`npm install -g agent-browser`), and captured at a proxy this
binary runs: every request is policy-checked and written down
before it moves.

### The websec workbench

`h5i-websec` is a separate archive, and installing it is a
deliberate act:

```bash
curl -L https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/releases/download/v0.5.6/h5i-websec-v0.5.6-<TARGET>.tar.gz | tar -xz
h5i plugin install websec --from ./h5i-websec
```

It holds no privilege of its own: every verb runs the `h5i browser`
verbs a person would type, through the same policy, budget and
receipts.

### The recon ledger

`h5i-recon` is the other plugin, and it arrives the same way:

```bash
curl -L https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/releases/download/v0.5.6/h5i-recon-v0.5.6-<TARGET>.tar.gz | tar -xz
h5i plugin install recon --from ./h5i-recon
```

It records what a target exposes, where each candidate came from,
and which stored message confirmed it. Discovery only: a URL read
out of a bundle stays a candidate until a request answers for it,
and nothing here is called a vulnerability.

### Security regression tests

`h5i-test` replays repository-owned attack flows and hands their
evidence to repository-owned external oracles:

```bash
curl -L https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/releases/download/v0.5.6/h5i-test-v0.5.6-<TARGET>.tar.gz | tar -xz
h5i plugin install test --from ./h5i-test
h5i test .h5i-tests/tests --target http://localhost:3000
```

It writes JSON and JUnit. OpenAPI coverage is report-only unless
`--min-coverage` is explicitly supplied.

Every request it makes is checked against an allowlist — every
request and every redirect hop — and written to the log before any
bytes move. A request that is not in `h5i browser requests` did not
happen. What a box adds, with `--in`, is that the record gains a
witness outside the browser; on a bare host that part is not
claimed.

### Available targets

| Target | Platform |
|--------|---------|
| `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` | Linux x86_64 (static, glibc-free) |
| `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` | Linux arm64 (static, glibc-free) |
| `aarch64-apple-darwin` | macOS Apple Silicon (arm64) |
| `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | Windows x86_64 |

Intel Macs have no published build: Rosetta 2 translates x86_64 to
arm64, not the reverse, so the `aarch64-apple-darwin` archive will
not run there. Build from source instead:
`cargo install --git https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i`

Each archive is accompanied by a `.sha256` checksum file.


## What's Changed
* Koukyosyumei patch 1 by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/805
* fix clippy needless_range_loop by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/806
* Doc showcase by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/807
* Add a repository-root Lake package for Reservoir by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/808
* Integrate with speckit by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/810
* Update README.md by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/811
* Fix duplicate line in README.md by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/812
* improve mutant testing by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/813
* bump to 0.5.6 by @Koukyosyumei in https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/pull/814


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/h5i-dev/h5i/compare/

detail.readme:
# h5i

**h5i** (pronounced *high-five*) is an Axum-based Rust web framework built around application kernels that can be formally verified with Lean 4 and executed on servers, bare-metal embedded devices, and GPUs. It also provides integrated development infrastructure for red-teaming, security regression testing, and sandboxed AI agents. --- ## 1. Install ```bash # Add the Rust web framework cargo add h5i-app # Install the h5i CLI and development tools curl -fsSL https://h5i.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --websec --recon --test # AI agent integration (optional) npx skills add h5i-dev/h5i ``` --- ## 2. Verifiable Web Framework [`h5i-app`](crates/h5i-app/README.md) is a composable, Axum-based Rust web framework built around a verifiable application kernel. - **Kernel-based architecture**: Separate application logic from infrastructure to verify and optimize core behavior. - **Formal verification**: Translate Rust application logic into Lean 4 using [Aeneas](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas) and prove their properties. - **Temporal logic and model checking**: Verify safety, liveness, and fairness-dependent properties of Rust application kernels and system-level models using [Veil](https://github.com/verse-lab/veil). - **Automatic specification generation**: Generate Lean 4 specifications and proofs for common patterns, including database schemas, authorization, and storage operations (compatible with [spec-kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit)). - **Axum-compatible deployment**: Deploy applications to platforms supporting Axum, including Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, and Fly.io, without rewriting application logic. - **Multi-target execution**: Run application kernels across different execution environments: - **Servers**: Execute kernels on CPUs with Axum-based HTTP integration. - **Embedded systems**: Run kernels on bare-metal devices using a `no_std`, heap-free HTTP/1.1 server. - **GPUs**: Accelerate supported kernels with GPU execution while retaining CPU fallback. ```toml [dependencies] h5i-app = { version = "0.5.6", features = ["http", "postgres"] } ```

## 3. Development Infrastructure h5i provides a unified CLI for building, verifying, debugging, and security-testing web applications with AI agents. For example, you can run professional red-teaming simply by opening your favorite AI agent harness and saying "Audit `https://.com` with h5i." > The red-team, CI/CD, sandbox, and UI are framework-independent, so there's no need to adopt `h5i-app`. **CLI Examples** ```bash h5i app new counter && cd counter # Scaffold a new Rust web app h5i app extract # Extract Lean 4 models from Rust h5i app prove # Verify properties with Lean 4 h5i app mutate # Test proof sensitivity with mutations h5i browser open https://example.com # Browser automation: Open a webpage h5i browser click @e3 # Click an element by reference h5i websec requests # HTTP security testing: Inspect captured requests h5i websec replay req_42 --set query.id=456 # Modify and replay a request h5i recon crawl --max-requests 200 # Reconnaissance: Discover attack surfaces h5i test .h5i-tests/tests/auth.yaml --target https://staging.example.com # CI/CD: Run security tests h5i test --target https://staging.example.com --openapi openapi.yaml --min-coverage 80 # Enforce API coverage h5i box --name lab --profile browser # Sandbox: Create an isolated environment h5i box shell lab -- claude # Run Claude inside the sandbox ``` ## 4. Dashboard ```bash h5i ui # Dashboard: Launch the local web UI ```
